s1.text: As usual, our starting point is a random experiment, modeled by a probability space \((\Omega, \ms F, \P)\).

s2.text: So \( \Omega \) is the set of outcomes, \( \ms F \) the collection of events, and \( \P \) the probability measure on the sample space \( (\Omega, \mathscr F) \).

s3.text: In this section, we assume that we fixed random variable \( Z \) defined on the probability space, with values in \( \R \).
